firstMessage.rawMarkdown:
Per rule 6b, here is the code behind our paper-track writeup, "From localization to resolution: code graphs, embeddings and a Gemma 4 agent".

- Code (Apache-2.0): https://github.com/m-ibrahim-khalil/gemma4-graphswap (tag v1.0)
- Analysis notebook: https://www.kaggle.com/code/ibrahimkhalil09/gemma4-graphswap-analysis
- Results dataset: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/ibrahimkhalil09/gemma4-graphswap-results
- Rebuilt graph and embedding bundle: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/ibrahimkhalil09/gemma4-graphswap-bundles
- Writeup: https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/gemma-4-developer-agent-paper/writeups/new-writeup-1792781438181

We ran the agent end to end in the official harness with Gemma 4 31B, varying only the code graphs and embeddings behind the analyzer's tools, over two seeds against a pre-registered noise floor. On 24 tasks and then 60, no condition (grep instead of graph tools, regenerated embeddings, rebuilt graphs) moved resolution beyond the control's own seed-to-seed noise.

graphswap builds harness-compatible graphs from public upstream checkouts, embeds them with any sentence-transformers model and writes SHA-256 manifests, so you can swap bundles into the harness and check what ran. The repo holds per-task CSVs, figures and the pre-registration. Raw agent traces and competition task text are not included.
